response:
I read `budget.xlsx` and calculated the total expenses. The file's **Budget** sheet lists 12 line items under the **EXPENSES** section (rows 11–22, amounts in column C):

| Category | Subcategory | Amount |
|---|---|---|
| Housing | Rent/Mortgage | 1,500 |
| Housing | Utilities | 200 |
| Housing | Insurance | 150 |
| Transportation | Car Payment | 350 |
| Transportation | Gas | 150 |
| Transportation | Insurance | 100 |
| Food | Groceries | 500 |
| Food | Dining Out | 200 |
| Entertainment | Streaming | 50 |
| Entertainment | Hobbies | 100 |
| Savings | Emergency Fund | 500 |
| Savings | Retirement | 400 |

**Total expenses across all categories: 4,200** (1,850 + 600 + 700 + 150 + 900).

Note: the template places the Savings line items (Emergency Fund, Retirement) inside the EXPENSES section, so they are included in this total; the Income section (Salary, Side Business, Investments, Other = 6,150) is not part of expenses. The workbook's own "Total Expenses" cell is blank, so the total is computed directly from the line-item amounts.
